title: Clean Element-Id Introduction System
description: Replace the introduction ("glass walkthrough") system's anchor/cutout model with a clean element-id model: each step declares introduce: Option<ElementId> (single element raised above the glass, pulses, anchors the info box) and show: Vec<ElementId> (additional interactive cutouts, no pulse), replacing the 9-variant IntroductionAnchor enum, IntroductionEmphasis, cutouts list, anchorFallbackSelectors, and additionalCutoutSelectors. Folded chrome is programmatically revealed (ids drive reveal: force-unfold action rail/utility bar, auto-open panel tab) instead of highlighting fold chips. A generalized data-element-alias channel lets non-semantic targets (first draggable catalogue row) get a stamped logical id. wgpu renderer brought to full parity: element-id-to-rect registry, veil-band cutouts, introduced pulse, reveal orchestration, advance-on-action/utility. advance stays semantic (Next|Action|Utility) — describes user behavior, not element targeting. Full design at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-every-single-ui-melodic-wirth.md. Builds on the prior UNIVERSAL-UI-ELEMENT-ID-SYSTEM ticket (closed) which established the element-id grammar this consumes.
summary:
Replaced the introduction ("glass walkthrough") system's anchor/cutout model with the clean element-id model end to end, and brought the wgpu renderer to full parity.

**Core contract** (framework/core/rs/lib.rs): deleted `IntroductionAnchor` (9-variant enum + `element_id()`) and `IntroductionEmphasis` entirely. `IntroductionStepDefinition` now carries `introduce: Option<String>` (raised above glass, pulses, anchors the info box) + `show: Vec<String>` (additional interactive cutouts, no pulse), plus `placement`/`advance`/`logos`. New authoring helpers: `UI_NAVBAR_ELEMENT_ID`, `UI_FOOTER_ELEMENT_ID`, `window_element_id()`, `panel_tab_element_id()`, `panel_tab_first_draggable_element_id()`. Mirrored in framework/core/js/index.ts (`windowElementId`, `panelTabElementId`, `panelTabFirstDraggableElementId`).

**Validation** (framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs): `validate_anchor` replaced with `validate_element_id` over `[introduce, ...show]` — grammar-valid ids are the escape hatch; declared utility/panelTab/window-action ids are checked against the app's own declarations.

**Authoring**: puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs (5 steps), mit-bestand/aggregator/brand.ts (7 German steps), .storybook/stories/ui/UIIntroduction.stories.tsx all rewritten to the new step shape using the new helpers.

**ui/js/react/index.tsx**: deleted the anchor-resolution/fallback-selector machinery entirely (`introductionAnchorSelector`, 3 fallback helpers, `IntroductionAnchorResolution`). New `elementIdSelector(id)` is the single resolver (`[id="${id}"], [data-element-alias~="${id}"]`). New generalized alias channel: `useFirstDraggableElementAlias` hook stamps a logical id onto the first draggable tree row in a panel, used by `Panel`/`MobilePanel`. `UIIntroduction` simplified to resolve `introduce`/`show` directly.

**framework/renderer/react/index.tsx**: anchor decomposition replaced by an id classifier that drives reveal — force-unfolds action rails/utility bar, auto-opens panel tabs — instead of highlighting fold chips.

**framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs full parity**: element-rect registry (`CHROME_ELEMENT_RECTS`) with registration at panel-tab bodies + tab-bar chip fallbacks, action rail rows (unfolded) + folded chip fallback, and utility buttons/toggles; `.firstDraggable` resolves via a live scan of `input.hit_targets` for the first draggable tree row inside the panel body. `chrome_tour_frame_begin` reveal orchestration (force-unfolds action rails via `action_panel_folded`, expands nested utility collections via new `utility_collection_path_to_id`, opens+selects panel tabs), latched per step id so user-initiated re-folding sticks. Advance-by-doing wired into `dispatch_action` (action) and `apply_set_active_utility` (utility, activation branch only; `HostEffect::SetActiveUtility` now funnels through it too). Keyboard: Escape skips, Enter/→ advances Next-only steps, ← goes back. i18n strings for Skip/Back/Next/Done/hints added to `shell_chrome_string`, byte-matching the React EN/DE bundle. Logo row rendering via the existing `resolve_ui_image`/`push_raster_quad` pipeline, dark-mode aware, skips un-cached logos.

**Three unrelated pre-existing bugs found and fixed** (blocking wgpu compilation for everyone, root-caused per CLAUDE.md's fix-at-the-root mandate):
1. `#[path = "../../../../plugin/registry/generated/hosts.rs"] mod generated_plugin_hosts;` was declared inside an inline `pub mod plugin_bridge { ... }` block. POSIX path resolution requires every directory component a `..` traverses — even one that's lexically cancelled — to physically exist; `plugin_bridge/` has no real directory on disk, so no number of `..`s could ever resolve it. Fixed by moving the `mod` declaration (with the correct 3-dot path) to the crate root and re-exporting via `pub use crate::generated_plugin_hosts::{...};` inside `plugin_bridge` to preserve the `crate::plugin_bridge::PluginHostConfig` API every call site depends on.
2. Four `ViewState` struct literals in the wgpu renderer were missing newer `window_id`/`window_instances`/`active_tool_id` fields (schema drift from concurrent work) — filled with `None`/`Vec::new()`/`None`.
3. `theme_is_dark` (in `engine_canvas`) and `resolve_ui_image` (in `interpreter`) were module-private, invisible to the `shell` module's new logo-rendering code — widened to `pub(crate)` and imported.

**Verification**: cargo test passing — framework-core (51), framework-plugin introduction (10), puzzle-plugin full suite (84), framework-renderer-wgpu chrome_overlays_tour (37, plus the whole crate now compiles clean). Typegen regenerated cleanly (no diff vs. hand-verified manifest). Targeted vitest passing — ui-react elementIdSelector (1), UIIntroduction (8), useFirstDraggableElementAlias (2); framework-renderer-react introduction (4). Full ui-react suite intentionally not run (known OOM, separate ticket INVESTIGATE-UI-REACT-VITEST-HEAP-OUT-OF-MEMORY). Manual dev-preview walkthrough not performed this session (native wgpu app + concurrent long compile cycles made it impractical); the unit-test coverage above exercises every new code path (reveal, advance-by-doing, keyboard, pulse, placement, veil bands, element-rect resolution) directly.
